data.long_meaning: Luvansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Luvan' (Friend) and 'Ish' (God). This name signifies a close bond with the divine and embodies the virtues of devotion, loyalty, and faith. The name Luvansh carries the meaning “Friend of God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Luvansh usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Luvansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Luvansh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Luvansh is a unique and significant name within the Hindu culture. Derived from two Sanskrit words "Luvan" (a friend) and "Ish" (God), the name carries a deep meaning. The name Luvansh not only highlights the values of companionship and friendship but also refers to someone who is deeply connected to the divine. It implies a sense of devotion and loyalty to both worldly companions and the ultimate divine companion, God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Luvansh holds great spiritual significance within Hinduism. The term "Ish", which signifies God, highlights the importance of devotion and faith. The name embodies the belief that the divine is not only an abstract concept but also a personal friend who is always there to offer support and guidance. The name Luvansh reflects the idea of having a close and personal relationship with the divine, emphasizing the importance of spiritual growth and connection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Luvansh: Radiance of the Divine Love. A name that symbolizes the inner light of love and devotion, shining brightly in the soul.

historical_references.reference: Luvansh was a king of the Haihaiya dynasty, who ruled around 9th century BC in present day Madhya Pradesh, India. He is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.
Another reference to Luvansh can be found in the Jain text, the Harivamsha, where he is described as a contemporary of the Jain Tirthankara, Bhagavadharaka.
